name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.20.0 — `init.md` (604 lines, the last big English program standing after v7) is rewritten around one new script, `spec/scripts/init-gen.js` (`spec-paths init-gen`): `probe` reports read-only findings (`frontendDesign`, `testCommand`, `atRisk`) and always exits 0 on adverse findings — findings are data, never a probe failure; `generate` reads a session-authored profile JSON and becomes the sole writer of every grounding-layer deliverable (config, pipeline rules file, convention rules, agents, both skills, settings permissions merge, patterns script, manifest), enforcing manifest-check.sh-then-stamp ordering in code — a red manifest-check now structurally cannot leave a stamped config, closing a rule that was previously prose an interrupted session could violate. A spike falsified the locked `.claude/worktrees` idempotency check (`git check-ignore -q .claude/worktrees` exits 1 on a fresh host when the directory does not yet exist, even with the ignore entry present); the script probes a child path instead, and a test pins the corrected form. An existing target file that differs from what the profile would produce now refuses generation at exit 3 (nothing written) unless `--refresh` is passed, with `.claude/settings.json` always merge-preserving in both modes — re-running init can no longer silently clobber hand-edits; an existing settings file that does not parse as JSON is refused in pre-flight at exit 2 with nothing written (found at review 2026-08-23: the merge previously swallowed the parse error and rebuilt the file, destroying the host's permission allow AND deny entries at exit 0 with no warning). Three probes brief 11 named land: `frontend-design` install detection via `claude plugin list --json` (ADR-0001 — the script only detects, the interview only offers, the user only consents, with a typed `unavailable` fallback to asking directly), the `testCommand` no-match probe (the class behind the 2026-08-20 at-risk escape — a runner exiting 0 on a nonexistent path now surfaces in the interview and, once accepted, lands a permanently re-verifiable negated-`exec` manifest row), and `scope-reconcile.js`'s additive `--probe-at-risk` mode (its existing `--json`/`--dirs` modes byte-identical, pinned) disclosing when the at-risk review leg will likely never fire on a host. `tests/run-ledger.test.js`'s prose pin over init.md retargets to a behavioral test now that the union-driver instruction lives in code, not prose. 7.19.0 — a review that burns its fix loop to the cap (2 iterations) and is then abandoned no longer writes zero ledger rows: the cap refusal now appends an **escalate row** at the moment of the refusal, an honestly-derived non-CLEAN verdict carrying `escalated: true`, minted by `verdict.js` behind a new `--escalated` flag with `--fixDispatched 0` (the dispatched fix never landed; refused with `--fixDispatched > 0` or `--profile release`, and refused rather than printed when the derivation reaches CLEAN under evidence drift — a self-contradictory CLEAN+escalated row is the worst possible output the one file that must never wrongly say CLEAN could carry). `spec-review-driver.js`'s `writeEscalateRow()` runs the pass from `handleFixApplied()`'s cap branch before dying, reusing spec 04's stopped-ledger durability verbatim in a worktree (`<mainRoot>/.claude/spec-runs.stopped.jsonl`, drained into the tracked ledger at close positioned before the close row) and self-healing a missing append on a bare re-invocation via the sidecar's `escalateRunId` mark. The ESCALATE step text now names both exits — fresh dispositions (`--fix-dispatched 0` covering the pool) closing normally through the waive/reject route, or deleting the `<spec>.review/` sidecar to abandon and restart cold — plus the absolute path the row landed in; a new driver-entry detector warns (stderr-only, never blocking) when a sidecar-recorded durable path no longer has a readable row for the spec+runId. `spec/commands/review.md`'s ledger-append sentence now names ESCALATE alongside STOPPED and CLOSE, and its ESCALATE re-entrancy prose names the row and both exits. No new verdict word: the escalation fact rides as a typed row field, never a second place that derives or asserts CLEAN. 7.18.0 — a foreign test's skip line now maps through to the owning spec's `[env:]` sanction on the realistic path: `ac-matrix.js` gains a third mapping route, tried only after both existing routes miss, that reads the runner's own file qualifier off a `<relpath>::<name>` skip line and takes that file's full-token AC-ID citations as `mappedIds`, feeding the existing sanction logic unchanged; every edge (no qualifier, path outside root, missing file, zero citations) fails closed to today's `unmapped-skip`, and `spec-review-driver.js`'s SKIPS prompt now instructs qualifier retention so the route has evidence to read. `smoke.sh` adds a pre-boot staleness probe: if `readyCheck` already passes before `bootCommand` is spawned, it prints `__SMOKE_FAIL__ stale-ready` naming the remedy and exits a new documented code 7 instead of booting into an environment it can't attribute readiness to (previously observed as exit 143 / `shutdown-unclean` when an orphaned prior process faked instant readiness). Separately, D5's reopen condition from 20260817/05 fired: `ac-matrix.js`'s coverage grep and `red-check.js`'s carried-AC classifier both did bare-substring AC-ID matching, so `AC-…-1` phantom-matched inside `AC-…-12` — coverage failed OPEN (4 laundered ACs across a 78-spec scan) and red-check failed CLOSED (a false `unsanctioned-green` that stopped specs/20260822/02's build same-day). Both call sites now go through one exported `lib/spec-sections.js` helper, `acIdOccurs(text, id)` — full-token by boundary check, no per-call RegExp — so a prefix hit neither launders coverage nor stops a build; the four historically-laundered ACs get `/spec:escape` rows against their owning reviews as separate recorded audit work, not silent repair.
